verdict.root_cause: Three minutes before onset, platform-automation attached a traffic-shaping container to cartservice's network namespace with a fixed 300ms egress delay, zero jitter, on eth0 [tr_3a465198ab35]. Every packet leaving that interface now carries the penalty, so each Redis round trip and each gRPC response is delayed. Traces measure exactly that quantum and show it scaling per Redis call, not per request: single-Redis GetCart/EmptyCart ~302ms, two-Redis AddItem ~603ms, with cartservice self-time sub-millisecond [tr_f503592247fe]. Non-cart dependencies in the same slow checkout traces stay single-digit milliseconds, and cartservice logs show continuous healthy serving with no errors or restarts [tr_eb19ac22327d, tr_8ae72b281f61]. frontend and checkoutservice alerted because they wait on the inflated cart hops [tr_8cd345d44250].
verdict.reasoning: The change record names a quantified mechanism (300ms fixed netns egress delay) landing ~3 minutes before onset [tr_3a465198ab35], and the traces independently measure that same quantum per network round trip rather than per request [tr_f503592247fe]. A per-request floor, application CPU/GC work, a read-only cache problem, and a shared downstream fault were each ruled out on that trace evidence. Logs rule out crash, restart and resource exhaustion at the cart tier [tr_eb19ac22327d, tr_8ae72b281f61]; the only image changes reverted to baseline 13 minutes before onset, ruling out bad_deploy [tr_3a465198ab35]. The failure callers experience is waiting, so the class is dependency_latency and the fix is removing the shaping rule rather than rolling back an artifact.
open_questions: frontend's error-ratio change point is 04:25:30, about 19 minutes before the shaping container was created [tr_8cd345d44250]; that earlier elevation is unexplained and may be a separate concurrent issue.

No trace samples exist between 02:59 and 04:49:29 [tr_f503592247fe], so latency onset is bracketed only to that interval and is not itself pinned to the change; Loki truncation left 04:47:30 uncovered [tr_eb19ac22327d, tr_8ae72b281f61].

cartservice span-metrics are empty in both windows [tr_f0b0f3d1b9e8], so cart-side error rate is unobserved; nor is it established whether the shaping container is still attached or why automation created it.

alternatives.root_cause: The Redis backing store for carts became slow, adding ~300ms to every HGET and HMSET.
alternatives.why_not: Redis-side slowness would not also add ~302ms to the caller's hop above the cartservice server span [tr_f503592247fe], and no change record names Redis while one names a 300ms injection at cartservice's interface [tr_3a465198ab35].

alternatives.root_cause: An unrelated fault starting near 04:25 is driving frontend errors, and the cart latency is a later, secondary effect.
alternatives.why_not: The slow checkout traces attribute nearly all root latency to the two cart hops with every other dependency fast [tr_f503592247fe]; no dispatch identified any frontend-side mechanism, leaving this only as an unexplained timing discrepancy.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The corrective action the evidence actually points to — detaching or deleting the platform-automation traffic-shaping container that holds a fixed 300ms/0ms-jitter egress delay on eth0 in cartservice's network namespace [tr_3a465198ab35] — is not in this system's allowlist. If a human performs that detachment out-of-band, the observable confirmation would be cartservice server spans in Tempo returning from ~302ms (single-Redis GetCart/EmptyCart) and ~603ms (two-Redis AddItem) to the pre-onset 0.2-5.7ms range seen at 02:38 and 02:59 [tr_f503592247fe], within about two minutes of the detach.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if one of the three permitted actions would in fact clear the delay. Specifically, recreating cartservice's container (rollback_image or restart_service) would give it a new network namespace, potentially orphaning the shaping attachment — that is a plausible side effect, but it is not what either action's preconditions describe, and nothing on this board tests it. It is also wrong if a prior cartservice configuration containing the shaping parameters is recorded somewhere I was not shown; the change history explicitly says otherwise (no config or env-var entries in the window, only container-create and image update/revert events) [tr_3a465198ab35]. Falsifying observation: a change-history entry naming a config or flag value for cartservice inside the window, or a confirmed record that the shaping container is already detached (in which case the residual ~300ms would have some other cause and any action here is misdirected).
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves the 300ms-per-Redis-round-trip penalty in place, so checkout latency stays at ~2.5s root and frontend keeps shedding requests at the elevated rate [tr_f503592247fe, tr_8cd345d44250]. That is a real ongoing cost, accepted deliberately. The alternative risks are worse-matched: revert_config fails its stated precondition outright — the change history for the window contains no configuration or environment-variable entries, only a container creation and image update/revert pairs [tr_3a465198ab35] — so there is no prior configuration to restore and the action would either no-op or restore an unrelated baseline while recreating the container. rollback_image would redeploy an image tag that the evidence already places at pre-window baseline at onset (both hotfix updates were reverted, the last 13 minutes before onset) [tr_3a465198ab35], so it changes nothing causal while resetting connections. restart_service requires evidence of bad process state, and the logs show continuous healthy serving with no errors, panics or restart banners [tr_eb19ac22327d, tr_8ae72b281f61] — process state is demonstrably fine.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing is being changed. The population that continues to see the existing degradation is frontend and checkoutservice, which wait on the inflated cart hops and are already alerting [tr_8cd345d44250, tr_f503592247fe], and through frontend the loadgenerator traffic. Had any of the container-recreating actions been taken, the blast radius would have been cartservice plus a connection reset visible to its inbound callers frontend and checkoutservice. Two open gaps argue for a human eye before anything is done: frontend's error-ratio change point at 04:25:30 sits ~19 minutes before the shaping container was created [tr_8cd345d44250] and is unexplained, and cartservice span-metrics are empty in both windows [tr_f0b0f3d1b9e8], so cart-side error rate cannot be used to confirm recovery — latency traces are the only usable confirmation channel.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting in sequence starting at cartservice and spreading through frontend and checkoutservice is a propagating failure, not a single quiet warning. Ordering suggests a shared downstream dependency or cart backend degradation.
